                    ### Question
                    A 45-year-old woman gravida 1, para 1, comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of a right breast lump and a 4.5-kg (10-lb) weight loss. She has not had any breast pain or nipple discharge. She had right breast mastitis 10 years ago while breastfeeding but has no other history of serious illness. Palpation of the right breast shows a 3-cm firm mass with well-defined margins lateral to the right nipple . There is dimpling of the overlying skin but no rash. The left breast is normal. A mammogram shows a density with calcifications in a star-shaped formation in the same location of the mass. Histological examination of a biopsy specimen from the breast mass is most likely to show which of the following?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Dilated ducts lined with neoplastic cells and necrotic centers
opb. Disorganized nests of glandular cells with surrounding fibrosis
opc. Large, pink-staining cells in the epidermis
opd. Orderly rows of monomorphic cells that do not stain with E-cadherin
ope. Infiltration of ductal cells blocking the dermal lymphatics

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The clinical presentation of a right breast lump with dimpling, weight loss, and mammographic findings of star-shaped calcifications raises suspicion for malignancy, likely invasive ductal carcinoma. The histological examination of such a mass typically shows disorganized nests of glandular cells with surrounding fibrosis, consistent with invasive ductal carcinoma. The option indicating 'Dilated ducts lined with neoplastic cells and necrotic centers' is more characteristic of ductal carcinoma in situ rather than invasive disease. The presence of orderly rows of monomorphic cells that do not stain with E-cadherin suggests lobular carcinoma, which is less likely given the clinical context. The infiltration of ductal cells blocking the dermal lymphatics is indicative of inflammatory breast cancer, which is not supported by the current findings. Therefore, the most likely histological finding is 'Disorganized nests of glandular cells with surrounding fibrosis.'
